name: Dixon Technologies (India) Ltd
about: Dixon Technologies (India) Limited,  incorporated  in  1993 ,  is  a  Electronic  Manufacturing  Services  (EMS)  company  with operations in the electronic products vertical such as consumer electronics, lighting, home appliance, closed-circuit television cameras  (CCTVs), and mobile  phones. It also  undertakes reverse logistics operations.  Besides, it manufactures security surveillance equipment, wearables & audibles, AC-PCBs. Recently, it has entered a JV with Imagine Marketing Private Limited for designing and manufacturing wireless audio solutions in India. [1]

sections.one_liner: India's largest smartphone EMS. Key now: Q1 FY27 margin fell to 3.0%, and reported profit leans on fair-value gains.
business: EMS maker of phones, telecom gear, IT hardware, appliances, TVs and lighting, backward-integrating into camera modules and displays. [AR FY26]
Mobile & EMS was Rs14,179cr of Rs15,557cr Q1 FY27 revenue (91%). That figure appears to include telecom Rs2,100cr and IT Rs1,350cr. [Q1FY27 call]
Q1 segment margins: mobile 2.6% (373/14,179), consumer electronics 5.9% (58/987), home appliances 8.4% (32/382). The mix is dominated by the thinnest segment. [Q1FY27 call]
Grows through JVs: Inventec 60:40, Signify 50:50, Imagine 50:50 and Longcheer 74:26, with Vivo pending. Minority leakage rises with each JV. [AR FY26]
financial_snapshot: Q1 FY27: revenue Rs15,548cr (+21% YoY) but EBITDA Rs463cr (-4% YoY). OPM was 3.0% vs 3.8% a year ago. [Numbers]
Reported Q1 PAT was Rs718cr, but excluding fair-value gains and minority it was Rs218cr. About 70% of reported profit is non-operating. [Numbers][Q1FY27 call]
TTM revenue Rs51,586cr, EBITDA Rs1,846cr, margin 3.6%. Screener ROCE 29.2% and ROE 18.9%; management cites 34.1% and 23.4%. [Numbers][Q1FY27 call]
Market cap Rs67,643cr at 36x P/E and 14.4x book. On FY26 adjusted PAT of Rs845cr, P/E is about 80x. [Numbers][Q4 FY26 call]
trajectory: Revenue CAGR was 58.9% over 3 years and 49.9% over 5 years. Growth stalled at +2.1% YoY in Dec-25 and Mar-26 before Q1's +21%. [Numbers]
EBITDA CAGR was about 53% over 3 years (519→1,873), slightly below revenue growth. OPM slid from 4.5% (FY21) to 3.8% (FY26) to 3.0% (Q1 FY27). [Numbers]
Reported PAT CAGR of 86% over 3 years overstates growth. FY26 reported PAT was Rs1,644cr vs management's adjusted Rs845cr. [Numbers][Q4 FY26 call]
FY27 volume guide was cut from 55-60M units (Oct-25) to 32-33M (May-26). Growth now depends on 12-15% price increases and non-mobile segments. [Q2 FY26 call][Q4 FY26 call]
balance_sheet: Borrowings more than doubled, from Rs453cr (FY23) to Rs994cr (FY26). Net worth rose faster, to Rs4,677cr, so D/E fell from 0.35 to 0.21. [Numbers]
Cash conversion cycle was -7 days in FY26: debtors 49 days and inventory 31 days imply about 87 payable days. Supplier credit funds the operation. [Numbers]
Net debt was Rs246cr at Dec-25. FY26 capex was Rs1,058cr, with display and camera capex still ahead. [Q3 FY '26 call][Q4 FY26 call]
cash_quality: CFO/PAT is 1.08x over 3 years on reported PAT. On adjusted PAT, FY26 CFO of Rs1,782cr is 2.1x the Rs845cr. [Numbers][Q4 FY26 call]
FCF was lumpy: Rs276cr, Rs16cr, Rs254cr, then Rs724cr in FY23-26. The cumulative Rs1,270cr is only 36% of reported PAT of Rs3,507cr. [Numbers]
Operating profits turn into cash; the fair-value gains do not. Value the company on CFO and adjusted PAT, not the 36x headline P/E. [Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: Management says memory costs are a 'pass-through, no absolute impact' (Jan-26). But Q1 EBITDA fell 4% YoY on 21% revenue growth. [Q3 FY '26 call][Numbers]
Return metrics diverge: management cites FY26 ROCE of 44.8%; screener shows 29%. ROE is 28.1% vs 18.9% at Q1. The definitions need reconciling. [Q4 FY26 call][Numbers]
Telecom FY27 guide fell from Rs7,500-8,000cr to Rs6,700-7,000cr. Yet Q1's Rs2,100cr annualises to Rs8,400cr, implying a sharp slowdown later in the year. [Q4 FY26 call][Q1FY27 call]
The margin-recovery date keeps slipping: FY27 component uplift (Oct-25) is now FY28. OPM is 3.0%, versus a 4-4.5% target at Rs1 lakh crore revenue. [Q2 FY26 call][Q1FY27 call]
guidance: FY27 revenue of about Rs56,000cr excluding Vivo, up 15-17%. Rs40,450cr is needed over Q2-Q4, about +12% YoY. [Q4 FY26 call]
Q2 FY27 smartphone volumes +20-25% QoQ; FY27 volumes 32-33M; Vivo JV revenue from Q3 FY27. [Q1FY27 call]
FY27 mobile margin of 2.8-3.2% excluding component PLI; group margin improvement only in FY28. [Q3 FY '26 call][Q1FY27 call]
IT hardware above Rs4,000cr in FY27 (about 3x); telecom Rs6,700-7,000cr; lighting Rs1,700cr. [Q4 FY26 call][Q1FY27 call]
Display mass production from end-Q3 or Q4 FY27; camera modules from 70M to 190M units in 15-18 months; Rs1 lakh crore revenue in 3-4 years. [Q1FY27 call][Q3 FY '26 call]

bull: Negative cash cycle (-7 days) and Rs724cr FY26 FCF after Rs1,058cr capex: growth is largely self-funded at 0.21 D/E. [Numbers]
Non-mobile run-rate is building: Q1 IT hardware of Rs1,350cr annualises to Rs5,400cr, above the Rs4,000cr guide; appliances earn 8.4% margins. [Q1FY27 call]
Display, camera modules and PLI 2 (2.5-5% export incentive) could lift mix-driven margins in FY28. Vivo JV is upside not in the Rs56,000cr guide. [Q1FY27 call][Q4 FY26 call]
bear: Adjusted P/E is about 80x (FY26 Rs845cr) for an EMS business whose OPM fell to 3.0% and whose Q1 EBITDA declined YoY. [Numbers][Q4 FY26 call]
Management credibility on guidance is weak: FY26 volumes missed by about 20%, the FY27 volume guide was nearly halved, and the telecom guide was cut within 3 months. [Q2 FY26 call][Q1FY27 call]
Mobile is 91% of revenue at 2.6% margin. PLI expiry costs 50-70bps, Q Tech is below 6-8%, and minority leakage grows with JVs. [Q1FY27 call][Q4 FY26 call]
questions: What generated the roughly Rs500cr Q1 fair-value gain, and will it recur?
Reconcile your 44.8% ROCE with the reported 29%: what capital is excluded?
Q1 telecom was Rs2,100cr; why guide only Rs6,700-7,000cr for FY27?
If memory costs pass through, why did Q1 EBITDA fall 4% YoY?

strategy: Scale EMS manufacturing platform across mobile, telecom, IT hardware, home appliances

Localise BOM; reduce import dependence for supply-chain resilience
Diversify customer base; expand into higher-value premium segments
annual_report.outlook: Long-term India electronics opportunity supported by global supply diversification, increasing localisation, and PLI/ECMS government policies expected to drive sustainable profitable growth despite near-term challenges.
